newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: RUGBY UNION-S. AFRICA MAKE FIVE CHANGES FOR LAST TEST.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-S. AFRICA MAKE FIVE CHANGES FOR LAST TEST.

text.p: With the series already lost, South Africa have made five changes and included two new caps in their team to take on the British Lions in the third and final test in Johannesburg on Saturday.
South Africa went 2-0 down in the series after missing six out of six kicks at goal in the second test in Durban last Saturday which condemned them to an 18-15 defeat.
Coach Carel du Plessis has responded by axing fly-half regular Henry Honiball -- one of three kickers tried on Saturday -- and brings in place-kicking specialist Jannie de Beer.
De Beer leapfrogs several other candidates for the number 10 jersey purely on the strength of his goal-kicking for Free State.

The 26-year-old once scored 48 points for South African Students against Taiwan. He was also successful with six out seven kicks and scored a try in claiming 20 points in Free State's 52-30 defeat by the Lions last Tuesday.
"He is a specialist goalkicker and we are giving him the opportunity to show his value and his worth at this level," said du Plessis on Monday.
"It's important that we look at goalkicking ability."
The second newcomer is de Beer's Free State colleague, flanker Johan "Rassie" Erasmus, 24, who is a straight replacement for Ruben Kruger who was injured in Saturday's test.

Also included because of injury is Krynauw Otto -- who was selected for the first test of the season against Tonga only to miss out through injury. He gets his chance in place of lock Mark Andrews who has had a recurrence of a back problem.
Du Plessis also made two changes in the front row, dropping prop Adrian Garvey and hooker Naka Drotske to the bench and promoting Dawie Theron and James Dalton.

"I just believe they deserve a chance to perform in the test lineup," explained du Plessis although he may have been prompted by concerns that the much heavier Springbok front row were unable to seriously discomfort their Lions opponents.
One feature of the new look South African selection is that the numbers 10 to 14 have just 12 caps between them.
Du Plessis added: "I believe we are committed to the team policy which is to give the younger players the chance to play when they deserve it."
The Lions are expected to name their team on Thursday.

South Africa - 15-Andre Joubert; 14-Andre Snyman, 13-Percival Montgomery, 12-Danie van Schalkwyk, 11-Pieter Rossouw; 10-Jannie de Beer, 9-Joost van der Westhuizen; 8-Gary Teichmann (captain), 7-Andre Venter, 6-Johan Erasmus, 5-Krynauw Otto, 4-Hannes Srydom, 3-Dawie Theron, 2-James Dalton, 1-Os du Randt.
Replacements: Russell Bennett, Boeta Wessels, Werner Swanepoel, Fritz van Heerden, Naka Drotske, Adrian Garvey.
